changes.reason: Added the explicit distinction that firm scoring happens before ordinary scoring and applies whether Company survives or fails; stated the separate Company failure scoring.
Named the designer and date supplied by the summary for the ruling, preserving its Foreign Invasion order closure distinction.
Added all ship storm-check eligibility, dice outcomes and sunk-ship destination required by the question.

answers.answer: 1. London Season — Attrition: “Simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.” A retiring member moves to Pensioners, the office card flips into Vacant Offices, and its fatigue returns to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.
answers.evidence: London Season > Attrition: quoted operative sentence and retirement destinations.

answers.answer: 1. Only players who retired at least one pensioner may select or discard one London Season display card. They act in descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows, including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. “Do not replace a chosen/discarded card during selection. If the display becomes empty, immediately skip every remaining eligible player.” At the end, discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season > Retirements and Prestige: quoted card eligibility, order, tie breakers, display and pensioner procedures.

answers.answer: 1. At phase start, check where the opportunity marker was; then choose a main action, taking it once or twice if the marker already matched it, and place/move the marker onto the chosen action. After that, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; it is never doubled and never moves the marker. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the doubled Writer action places three writers total: the action’s additional writer applies once that turn.
answers.evidence: Family: numbered opportunity-marker steps and Enlist Writer row.

answers.answer: 1. After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both remain. Pieces in Court are Company shares. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. Seeking a share places a member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pays the listed queue cost (£2, £3, £3, £4 or £5) to the bank; “Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.”
answers.evidence: Family > Seek Share row and New Company shares paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that member into the office; its owner gets the card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert its old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. For own-family hiring, verbal consent is required from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip that office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from Nepotism consent.
answers.evidence: Hiring: vacancy order, promotion/fatigue and skipped-office paragraph; Nepotism table and exceptions.

answers.answer: 1. The former Chairman first announces how many shares are needed for a pure majority (more than half of current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one winner’s Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. That piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms. If nobody gets support, the former Chairman picks any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, a prize (losing that prize’s VP); if impossible, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Chairman election paragraph, including fallback and Chairman share status.

answers.answer: 1. For a Company-office success check, first commit resources/cash; all cash comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office’s actions, returns the officeholder to supply, discards fatigue and flips the card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures can modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.
answers.evidence: Company Operation > Success checks paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares, with the Chairman counting; never pass the Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting total borrowing limits. Cash already in offices remains there for their use.
answers.evidence: Actions > Chairman.

answers.answer: 1. The Manager of Shipping must spend treasury funds until £2 or less remains. Lease an extra ship for £2; fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner’s consent; buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Actions > Manager of Shipping.

answers.answer: 1. A President declares regions for Trade, including the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one per declared nonhome region. Failure can be retried during operations if affordable, but each President can have at most one successful Trade per turn, and failed attempts/retries remain that President’s uninterrupted opportunity. A successful Trade has capacity of one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone and does not exhaust ships. Fill as many as possible in declared regions: first writer goes to home port; every later order extends the connected route filled during this same Trade. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend the route; writers do not limit capacity, so use all writers then continue using filled-order tokens for remaining ships. No President may fill another President’s home region, even if vacant. Balance rises by each order’s printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn. The President gets £1 from the bank per order and writer owners get £1 per placed writer.
answers.evidence: Actions > Presidency operations and Trade: declaration, check, success cap, capacity, route, protected home regions, revenue and bonuses.

answers.answer: 1. A Commander may target their own Presidency’s home, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another home region or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhaust each chosen officer or regiment for one die and each local alliance for its printed dice; subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once. Company defense strength is zero. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for officer losses.
answers.evidence: Actions > Commanders and Deploy, steps 1–3.

answers.answer: 1. On success, take loot from the bank equal to £4 per target tower plus any faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of surviving participating officers used in that attempt plus one for the Commander. Count only that attempt’s surviving participating officers and used regiments/alliances. Repeatedly distribute £1 to the Commander family for the Commander plus each of their used surviving officers, then £1 per used surviving officer to other families clockwise, then £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece to the bank, repeating that cycle until loot is gone. The Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower and dome, remove every matching empire flag throughout India if the target was a capital, open all target orders and remove all unrest; on a new conquest, turn the control token symbol-side up above the associated President’s box, put the Governor overlay in the region and only the Governor card in Vacant Offices. If the Elephant faced outward from the conquered region, move it fully inside. On catastrophe, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up and the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and there is no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Actions > Commanders and Deploy: loot formula, payout table, control steps and catastrophe paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Take the Governor’s printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one option: build one stage of a Company ship, commission a regiment into the Army associated with the Governor’s President, or add an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President’s treasury. Each Tax after the first this turn adds regional unrest. Every unsuccessful roll adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Repeat with the shrinking pool until choosing to stop, no dice remain, or catastrophe.
answers.evidence: Actions > Governors: Administer, result and option tables.

answers.answer: 1. Company expenses are £1 per existing Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones, including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans. Each loan advances Debt one only while a track space remains; at maximum Debt, keep taking loans without advancing Debt further. Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra expense this turn. After emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations under current Standing and lower Standing one if it is below them. After that, the Chairman may pay affordable dividends costing one cash per Company share and paying each owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one.
answers.evidence: Revenue > Company expenses, expectations and dividends.

answers.answer: 1. An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary Crisis first, then secondary regions in Bombay → Madras → Bengal Army order; within each Presidency its Commander chooses the order of associated regions. A normal primary Crisis attack strength includes the normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in its target. A primary Foreign Invasion uses only the ordinary attack die; every secondary Rebellion uses only the unrest cubes in that secondary region. If the associated Commander is occupied, that Commander chooses and exhausts pieces and normal trophy gains/losses apply; if Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in its stead without trophies; if both Commander and Military Affairs are vacant, Chairman chooses without trophies. Exhaust active Army pieces equal to Crisis strength, or as many as possible. The attack fails and defense succeeds only if newly exhausted pieces equal Crisis strength: remove all attacked-region unrest and the Commander gains one trophy; if this defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. If they do not equal the strength, attack succeeds and defense fails, causing Region Loss; successful primary Invasion also applies empire creation/growth. Local alliances cannot be split between purposes, but whether excess strength from an indivisible strength-2 alliance counts as equal to a strength-1 attack remains unresolved in the summary.
answers.evidence: Events > Attacks on Company and Mounting defense: attack order/strength and defense table; unresolved alliance-counting boundary.

answers.answer: 1. A result of -1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma’s “If Failed” text, and the Opposition Leader returns the token and takes the PM dial; the new PM moves the proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. A result of zero or higher passes: place the law with passed laws, PM takes the passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then immediate law effects. Finally restore every card used for voting to regular orientation after either outcome. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament > Resolution paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting and its support threshold, but no policy accompanies the vote and the PM may vote against it. On passage, lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give PM a passed-law token and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token up to a maximum of ±3 VP per share; PM stays in power and the Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 starts deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation section and table.

answers.answer: 1. To form a firm, a player who currently manages none returns one eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to its invested side, flips their family board to its firm-charter side, places a family member as first firm share, sets the value cube to the leftmost track space and takes £5 from the bank into London. To invest in an existing firm, with manager consent, contribute a Company share or workshop in the same way to create a share and take £5 from the bank into London. At ten firm shares, later investments still add £5 but create no share. The Chairman share cannot be used; Company shares cannot be used at all when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; shares created this turn cannot be used even if traded away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested, give no bonus or Company-failure VP, and stay invested if the firm fails.
answers.evidence: Deregulation > treasuries paragraph; Firms phase > Form a firm and Invest.

answers.answer: 1. Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn, and only a firm with at least one ship may select a strategy; it may select a closed home port. Managers secretly and simultaneously choose a trade zone/home port and commit a secret London cash bid, or Hobnob. Reveal bids simultaneously, but keep strategy cards facedown until the matching Presidency begins. At that Presidency’s start, before actions, the matching firms reveal and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative equals ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), and a successful President’s Trade creates initiative the same way using Presidency ships. After that success, fill in lowest-initiative order; President chooses among tied traders. If President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commander/Governors had a chance, with Chairman choosing initiative ties. Fill only open orders, at most ships + 1, starting at strategy home port and tracing its own filled route back there. Each firm may fill a particular order only once and cannot refill its own earlier order; it may refill another firm’s or Company-filled order, and the Company may refill firms’ orders. An already filled order pays half listed revenue, rounded down. Trade revenue goes to India; advance firm Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury that turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade table/procedures.

answers.answer: 1. At the start of Revenue, before Company expenses, firms act in initiative order then other firms; ties go by manager’s most windows, then PM clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm value, paid using either or both London and India treasuries. If the firm cannot pay, it dissolves unless rescued: shares go to Debtor’s Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to shipyards, charter flips to family side, and workshops remain invested. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends from India treasury only; each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. Waiving payment requires both the shareholder’s choice and manager’s consent. Record total actual cash paid, not per-share dividend; an active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero, while Hobnob retains its prior marker. Sweep remaining India money into London.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends section.

answers.answer: 1. Components are limited; when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.
answers.evidence: Components > Limits.

answers.answer: 1. Negotiable items are enterprises, facedown blackmail, family treasury cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial and Chairman piece cannot be traded. To transfer a share, return the old owner’s family member and replace it at the share’s location with a member from the receiving family. Blackmail may be shown privately but must stay facedown when traded; played faceup blackmail cannot be traded.
answers.evidence: Special Rules > Negotiation table and share-transfer/blackmail paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. An immediate transfer is binding. A promise of future behavior is nonbinding, except a printed promise card’s guaranteed effect can be called if possible. Promise calls follow the card’s timing and limits, and no promise calls are allowed during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, the guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Promise cards may be transferred to a third party or back to their guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice; for example, a workshop paid this Bonuses phase does not pay again after a sale during that phase.
answers.evidence: Special Rules > Agreement/promise table.

answers.answer: 1. Use the selected scenario’s player setup cards, add three extra cards for five players or six for six, shuffle and deal evenly. Place every listed holding: take listed cash from the bank and enterprises into the player’s area; put each office’s family member into its office and give its matching office card to that owner; put Company-share members in Court; put writers, officers and trainees in their indicated Presidency/Army/Training boxes; put each Commander in that Army’s Commander slot without an office card; place each ship in its listed sea zone or on its shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together into one deck and deal three for the London display, with prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4.

answers.answer: 1. The game ends after the scenario’s final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure is normally immediate; if it occurs during Events in India, finish that phase before Final Scoring, and if legislation causes failure, finish the vote first. Once the game is over, stop negotiations, promise calls and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use. During all of Final Scoring, no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions opening paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Power counts enterprises and Company shares at their current Power-track rates (bottom two positions are zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for the PM, and printed card power, including faceup or facedown blackmail and applicable spouse. Most/second awards are 3/1 VP on final turns 1–3, 5/2 on turns 4–6, and 8/4 on turns 7–8. A tie for first awards only the lower award to each tied player; there is no other award. Tied second place gets no award. Highest final VP wins; ties go to most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Scoring > Power award and victory tie rules.

answers.answer: 1. If Company survived, add the Court’s current VP per Company share; if it failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. For a survived Company, final retirements roll office attrition and then retire Pensioners, with no prestige/display cards. If the Company failed, instead draw one random Company failure card and resolve its printed consequence. The firm special retirement step occurs before Power in either outcome and is not replaced by the failure card.
answers.evidence: Scoring > Court/workshops and Final retirements/failure card.

answers.answer: 1. Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions, and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise/share trades are made immediately upon taking the spouse. Retirement discounts can stack, are personal, and each can be used once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual spending and therefore display priority.
answers.evidence: London Season > Spouses and retirement discounts.

answers.answer: 1. If a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or an unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes available after the ship returns.
answers.evidence: London Season > Returned shipyard rule.

answers.answer: 1. Enlist Writer places a member in any Presidency’s Writers box; with at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer once this turn. Enlist Officer places a member in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury costs £4 to the bank and gives a luxury, 2 VP while owned and its window icon; it is a social enterprise. Purchase Shipyard costs £2 to the bank and places its matching ship unfitted on that shipyard; it is a shipping enterprise, gives one vote and a £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop costs £5 to the bank and gives a manufacturing enterprise, two votes, a £1 bonus, and 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. Seek Share puts a family member on an empty Stock Exchange space and pays the bank the space’s listed £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5; it is an applicant, not yet a share.
answers.evidence: Family action effects table.

answers.answer: 1. If a family must place a piece and has none in supply, take one from any of that family’s prizes and lose the prize’s printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no family action is possible, take none and return the opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Family: family-piece reuse and no-action rules.

answers.answer: 1. If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, taking a member from a prize and losing that prize’s VP. If return is impossible, there is no Chairman.
answers.evidence: Chairman election paragraph: empty Court fallback.

answers.answer: 1. Chairman election: shareholders elect using the majority procedure. The Chairman hires Director of Trade, choosing a current officeholder other than Chairman or Governor, or any writer if all offices are vacant; Commanders are not officeholders. The Chairman chooses any writer for Manager of Shipping. For Military Affairs, Chairman chooses a Presidential Commander, or if none, any officer, or if none, any Officer-in-Training. Director of Trade chooses a President who is a writer of that Presidency or a Governor associated with it. The associated President chooses a Governor from a writer or officer in the region; a Commander is not an officer and is ineligible. Chairman chooses any writer for China, hired immediately when created. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way. Ordinary own-family hires need verbal consent from every other player in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt.
answers.evidence: Hiring: Nepotism exceptions and Office/hirer/candidate table.

answers.answer: 1. The Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 from the Director’s treasury per die and taking no penalty. A successful check either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing the Superintendent overlay/card; Chairman immediately hires a writer. After all Envoys, the Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones, including China once created. The Director cannot transfer while still taking Envoys.
answers.evidence: Actions > Director of Trade.

answers.answer: 1. Military Affairs may make up to two transfers, each moving one officer or regiment from one Army to another while remaining in its top half. Then assign every Officer-in-Training to any Army’s top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if there is a vacancy or a family has more total pieces in an Army than the current Commander’s family, choose among families with the most pieces; move the chosen officer to Commander and return the previous Commander to the top as an officer. A tie with the current Commander’s family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.
answers.evidence: Actions > Military Affairs.

answers.answer: 1. Each President chooses the order of its Commander, Governors and Trade; each position may decline, and each finishes all its actions before the next begins. Trade can be before or after the Commander or any Governor, but cannot interrupt another position. If the President is vacant, the Chairman sets the order only; the Chairman cannot trade or approve local-alliance purchases.
answers.evidence: Actions > Presidency operations and Trade.

answers.answer: 1. Trade does not exhaust ships. At Refresh, writers on orders return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and Presidency dividers return to supply. Fitted player ships keep their fatigue.
answers.evidence: Actions > Presidency Trade capacity; Upkeep and Refresh table.

answers.answer: 1. At the start of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts, request the President’s treasury funds for any printed-price local alliances in the Army, and the President must approve. Move purchased alliances to the active top half. When used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to the bottom half; its strength is usable once that turn and cannot be split among more than one purpose. Refresh exhausts any unused active alliances too and does not reactivate them, unlike officers and regiments.
answers.evidence: Actions > Commanders and Deploy opening paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. For Deploy into an already Company-controlled region to reopen orders or clear unrest, Company defense penalty is zero; with no tower, gain zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, loot is the minimum of surviving participating officers plus one for the Commander, distributed normally.
answers.evidence: Actions > Commanders and Deploy: Company-region special case.

answers.answer: 1. Each successful Governor Build performs one stage. If there is no partial ship in the Governor’s region, that success places the partial ship there; if a partial ship is already there, that success completes it into the sea zone associated with the Governor’s President. The two stages require two successes total, and a partial ship has no other effect. A commissioned regiment is placed in the Army associated with the Governor’s President; it has officer-like strength, its loot is paid to the bank, and it causes no officer-loss rolls.
answers.evidence: Actions > Governors: Administer option table.

answers.answer: 1. China is created by a successful Special Envoy or by Envoy to China law; in either case the Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director of Trade may send ships there like any sea zone; China ships count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. China acts after Bengal.
answers.evidence: China Superintendent and Director of Trade sections; Company Operation sequence.

answers.answer: 1. After Bengal, China may attempt Trade only once, including a failed attempt, so it cannot retry. Roll one die per ship, but without an export icon in Company-controlled regions, do not attempt China Trade at all. On success, count export icons in all Company-controlled regions only: Company Balance receives £4 times the number of icons, and the Superintendent’s family receives £1 per icon from the bank. Export icons in non-Company regions do not count.
answers.evidence: China Superintendent section and payment table.

answers.answer: 1. When Governor General law creates the office, immediately make all Governors pensioners, remove their overlays and partially built Company ships, and return Governor/Director cards to the box. Replace Director of Trade with Governor General, preserving holder and fatigue, and place its ribbon overlay. No further Governors or overlays are created upon conquest; printed Company symbols indicate controlled regions. When regions are lost, skip Governor Elimination.
answers.evidence: Governor General section.

answers.answer: 1. Governor General first adds £3 to Balance per Company region. Then it may repeatedly attempt Govern, paying £1 from its treasury per die with no penalty. Every 6 rolled adds one unrest to each Company region, even on success; failure adds another unrest to every Company region. On success, add £1 per Company region and choose one benefit per region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone including China, place a regiment into any Army, or add £2 to Balance or any office treasury except its own while adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices this turn must add unrest to different regions. It may have at most one successful Govern per turn.
answers.evidence: Governor General section.

answers.answer: 1. Storms check only player-owned ships in affected sea zones, once per eligible ship: 1–2 causes nothing; 3–4 adds fatigue, or sinks an already fatigued ship; 5–6 sinks it. Company and extra ships are exempt. Ships assigned to China count as Eastern; firm ships count in the sea zone on their firm strategy; Hobnob firm ships are exempt. A sunk ship returns to its shipyard unfatigued.
answers.evidence: Events in India > Storms table and roll procedure.

answers.answer: 1. When an order newly closes, return any writer on it to its owner’s supply; flip a filled token to closed. If told to close an order in a region whose orders are already all closed, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to that region’s orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that connected region’s northernmost open order instead; if none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate a Cascade only once per event tile, but it can receive effects from multiple Cascades.
answers.evidence: Events in India > Closing orders and Cascades.

answers.answer: 1. Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the top-stack region; if all are closed, it Cascades. Windfall gives owners £1 per writer on orders in the top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle moves the Elephant, then shuffles that tile with the remaining draw stack and separately shuffles discards and places them on top; if the draw stack is empty, make the March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events in India event-procedure table.

answers.answer: 1. Leader gives one tower to the top-stack region if it is sovereign. If it is dominated, it instead rebels with the printed explosion modifier. Move the Elephant only if it was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events in India > Leader row.

answers.answer: 1. Peace opens orders connected across the Elephant’s border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If the Elephant is wholly inside a region instead, open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March the Elephant.
answers.evidence: Events in India > Peace row.

answers.answer: 1. For Invasion Crisis, the sovereign attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier must be strictly greater than the defender’s whole empire strength. On success, replace the defender’s flag with the attacker’s dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If the attacker had no empire, use a free capital/star flag and matching small flag; if none are available, no new empire or flags form. On failure, the attacker loses one tower.
answers.evidence: Events in India > Invasion Crisis.

answers.answer: 1. For Rebellion Crisis, compare only the rebelling region’s strength plus event modifier with its sovereign capital’s strength; other empire regions do not count. It must be strictly greater to succeed, so a tie fails. Success makes the actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed). Failure removes one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India > Rebellion Crisis.

answers.answer: 1. On Region Loss, the Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up and the Commander member returns to supply. Roll once per officer in the associated Army; each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate the Governor by returning its office card to the unused stack and its fatigue and member to supplies. Remove the Governor overlay, partial Company ship and unrest; restore the dome with one tower (or the Foreign Invasion specified strength) and the appropriate invasion flag. Return the control token to its region with £ loot side down and region-symbol side up; future conquest gets no loot modifier, and the region loses its Presidency association. A normal Invasion Crisis closes its orders or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion and Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals regions lost so far this turn: first −1, second an additional −2, and so on. One loss does not automatically lose any other Company region; resolve each other attack and defense separately.
answers.evidence: Events in India > Region Loss.

answers.answer: 1. After a successful Invasion Crisis, move the Elephant to the successful capital; after other Marches, move it to the top-stack region. In a Company region, place it fully inside. In a dominated region, point it toward its sovereign. In a sovereign region, point it across the shape-marked border on the tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by the actor, choose the first clockwise neighbor that is not; if all are dominated, use the redirect-arrow shape’s border, pointing toward the empire capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India > Elephant’s March.

answers.answer: 1. Foreign Invasion rolls the storm die to select targets: West means Bombay, South Madras and East Bengal; all storms means each, and no storms means the top-stack region. For each target, roll an ordinary die for attack strength and resolve an Invasion/Company attack. Unrest does not add to a Foreign Invasion’s primary attack strength or determine resulting tower levels; use the ordinary die for attack and halve that roll, rounded down, to create towers. On success, close all target orders once, Cascading if they were already all closed; remove the target’s flag and all matching flags if it was a capital, restore a dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half the attack roll rounded down. March with the circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded.
answers.evidence: Foreign Invasion event row and FAQ ruling.

answers.answer: 1. The PM must draw at least one law, revealing laws one at a time. After one or two ordinary, non-dilemma draws, the PM may stop or continue up to three total, then chooses any one revealed law and discards the others. Drawing a dilemma forces selection of that dilemma and ends drawing immediately. Before voting, PM moves the dial arm clockwise or counterclockwise, stopping at the first policy space matching the chosen law’s bottom icon; that space fixes the target and consequence.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets: drawing and policy selection paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. For Tax, each family pays £1 to the bank per target it owns; each unpaid target returns to supply, including Chairman if taxed. For Window tax, additionally pay each window on enterprises and each family member’s prize; return the enterprise/prize member if unable. For Bonus, the bank pays each family £1 per target it owns. For Power, swap the target Power marker with the next higher marker; if it is already highest, swap any other pair.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets > Policy table.

answers.answer: 1. Starting with the PM and going clockwise, players cast votes; each £1 family cash buys one vote, plus printed card votes. Each card’s votes can be used only once in the entire vote across all rounds: rotate it when used and leave it rotated until vote resolution, so it cannot vote in a later round. Adjust support up or down; tracks are unlimited. After each round PM may call another full round or stop. A round with no votes must end voting.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets > Voting.

answers.answer: 1. A player who voted for may later oppose; once opposed, they cannot vote for during that vote. Track opposition votes: the biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader, and a tied current holder retains it. With the recipient’s consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose, and count toward that person’s opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced use of the “Vote with my enterprises” promise.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets > Voting.

answers.answer: 1. Pay printed upkeep separately for each family member on a prize. If unpaid, return that member and lose the prize’s printed VP; negotiating help remains possible while the game continues. On the final turn, perform upkeep but skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. On nonfinal turns, return writers on orders to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, return filled tokens and Presidency dividers to supply, return extra ships to supply, reactivate exhausted Army officers and regiments, exhaust active local alliances without reactivating them, leave fitted player-ship fatigue as it is, and advance the Turn marker one turn before beginning London Season.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh paragraph and table.

answers.answer: 1. Each shareholder may make one additional retirement per London Season from supply rather than Pensioners, regardless of how many firms they own. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker of any firm in which they own a share; printed prize cost may exceed that marker when discounts cover the difference. No retirement is allowed from a firm with an absent or zero marker. Spouse discounts may enable a higher printed-cost prize, and retirement otherwise follows normal rules, including prestige eligibility. At the start of Final Scoring, score firms, then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success or failure, before Power or any ordinary final-scoring step; no display cards are used.
answers.evidence: Deregulation > Special retirement.

answers.answer: 1. A firm has London and India treasuries. The bank pays £5 per investment into London; London pays ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses. Trade revenue goes to India; India pays dividends and expenses. After dividends, remaining India money is swept into London. Investment cash comes from the bank to London; London cash cannot buy new equity shares, which require a Company-share or workshop contribution. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries; only specified investment, payout and expense procedures move firm money.
answers.evidence: Deregulation treasury paragraph; Firms phase investment, ship, trade and expenses/dividends rules.

answers.answer: 1. The Firms phase, when deregulated, comes after Family share creation and before Hiring. Investments are taken without set order until nobody wants more, then strategies are chosen. The manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm; the PM resolves conflicts between firms.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Firms phase: investments.

answers.answer: 1. A firm may fit a ship from its own or another player’s shipyard, but needs that shipyard owner’s consent and pays £3 from the firm’s London treasury to the bank. It may buy a player-owned ship already in the Company with the owner’s consent: £3 for an unfatigued ship or £2 for a fatigued ship, paid into the Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company ships or extra ships.
answers.evidence: Firms phase > Ships.

answers.answer: 1. Only a player who manages no firm at all may initiate a hostile takeover; managing a different firm makes the player ineligible. Obtain consent of holders of a majority of target-firm shares, then move the firm’s ships, money and shares to the player’s charter and copy both cube positions. The former manager returns the cubes and flips their board to its family side.
answers.evidence: Firms phase > Hostile takeover.

answers.answer: 1. A merger requires managers to negotiate with every shareholder’s consent. The highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied firms. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to the primary and return secondary boards to family sides. If the primary would exceed ten shares, return excess shares to their owners’ supplies with those owners’ consent. The primary’s value/dividend track remains the continuing firm’s track.
answers.evidence: Firms phase > Merger.

answers.answer: 1. Hobnob involves no bid, trade or dividends. The firm still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker for retirement. Hobnob firm ships are exempt from storms.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies Hobnob row; Firm expenses and dividends/storms paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. A firm at ten shares can still receive an emergency investment: emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules even when the ten-share cap prevents adding a share. Each emergency investment pays expenses, loses any remaining cash and lowers Value one space. The normal restriction also applies: shares created this turn cannot be used, even if traded away.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: emergency investments; Firms phase Invest restrictions.

answers.answer: 1. An emergency negotiated merger may involve only one other firm. The normal merger procedure still applies, including consent from every involved shareholder. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if it has not already done so, then cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: emergency merger paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders. Apply the insolvent-firm dissolution procedure: shares go to Debtor’s Prison, each worth −1 VP; ships return to their matching shipyards; and the charter flips to its family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Firms phase > Voluntary dissolution.

answers.answer: 1. During Final Scoring, for each player separately add VP from all shares across all their firms and round that player’s total down once, then deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor’s Prison. Firm shares score at Value 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3–4 = ½; 5–7 = 1; 8–9 = 1½; 10 = 2 per share. 2. This firm-scoring step occurs before special firm retirement and Power and applies whether the Company survives or fails. Company outcome separately determines Company-share and uninvested-workshop scoring: if Company survived, add the Court’s current VP per Company share; if it failed, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop.
answers.evidence: Scoring > Final Scoring order (“round that player’s total DOWN once”; firm scoring is step 1) and firm-track table; Court/workshops table.

answers.answer: 1. The five prizes are: cost £2, upkeep £0, 0 VP, 0 windows; £4, upkeep £1, 2 VP, 1 window; £8, upkeep £2, 4 VP, 2 windows; £14, upkeep £3, 8 VP, 3 windows; and £20, upkeep £4, 12 VP, 4 windows.
answers.evidence: Prizes per family member table.

answers.answer: 1. 1710 runs turns 1–5 and has no deregulation procedures. 1758 runs turns 3–7; the Company starts with monopoly and deregulation can be voted in. 1813 runs turns 5–8 and starts deregulated, allowing firms. Long 1710 runs turns 1–8, starts like 1710 and has deregulation available separately.
answers.evidence: Scenario scope and scenario figures tables.

answers.answer: 1. 1710 starts at £10 expectations and Debt 0, with £3 in each office treasury, Royal Protection, one regiment per Army and no Company ships. 1758 starts at £12 expectations and Debt 3, with £4 in each office treasury, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship in East Indian and the Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures table, including 1758 Bengal control-token note.

answers.answer: 1. 1813 starts on turn 5 with £10 expectations, Debt 0, £3 in each office treasury, Military Oversight, Deregulation on its Debtor’s Prison side and Calico Acts, two regiments per Army and one Company ship in each sea zone. Put the +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, return the Governor General law to the box and place its office overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors. The scenario card reverse supplies the exact India towers, flags, closed orders and Elephant.
answers.evidence: Scenario figures table and 1813 setup paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Power awards are 3 VP for most and 1 VP for second on final turns 1–3; 5 and 2 VP on turns 4–6; and 8 and 4 VP on turns 7–8. If first is tied, each tied player receives only the lower award and there is no other award. Tied second place receives none.
answers.evidence: Scoring > Power award.

answers.answer: 1. Initial Power positions are Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0 and Manufacturing 0. Standing expectations run £4/6/8/10/12/14/16; the reset S space is above £10. Deregulation lined spaces are Standing £4/6/8 and Debt 5/6/7/8; Standing £4 and Debt 8 are starred. In 1758 and Long 1710, PM may call the special vote if Standing and/or Debt is lined, and must call it if either is starred.
answers.evidence: Start Power positions and Deregulation condition paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Cole Wehrle clarified on April 30, 2023 that unrest does not add to a Foreign Invasion’s primary attack strength or determine its resulting tower levels. Use the ordinary die roll for attack strength and halving to create towers, and do not add the normal primary Crisis unrest. 2. On a successful Foreign Invasion, close all orders in the target region once; if they are already all closed, Cascade instead. Region Loss does not close them a second time; that additional closure is only for a normal Invasion Crisis.
answers.evidence: FAQ > Foreign Invasion and unrest (“unrest does not add”; “close all orders in the target region once”).

answers.answer: 1. Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reducing a check to zero dice means failure. Company Fraud is played at the start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice the highest roll (minimum zero), and take bank cash equal to the actual Balance reduction, so payout cannot exceed cash actually removed from Balance. Public Demands Impeachment returns the member to supply and the office card to vacancies. Military Oversight demotes one Commander to an officer, then appoints a Commander from officers; the same former Commander remains eligible to become Commander again.
answers.evidence: FAQ > Applicable official errata and Company Fraud payout-cap ruling.

answers.answer: 1. In shared setup, set Company Balance to £5, place Power tokens on their indicated starting positions, set family VP markers to zero and place loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Put local alliances in their named Army boxes and shuffle India events. Follow the chosen scenario card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and political map; set the Turn marker to its date and PM dial arm to the matching date. Copy the exact India towers, flags, closed orders and Elephant from the reverse of that scenario card.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–2 and scenario map setup paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. The normal turn order is London Season → Family → Firms (if deregulated) → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation votes happen at the very start of the turn before London Season. Skip London Season on the game’s first turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure.

answers.answer: 1. Retirements start with the Chairman, or the former Chairman if that office is vacant, then proceed clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize: pay its printed cost, move the member to the prize and gain its printed VP. Set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display-selection order, then pay the bank. Unused pensioners do not remain for another turn.
answers.evidence: London Season > Retirements.

answers.answer: 1. Whenever an empire loses its last dominated region, remove the surviving capital’s starred flag so it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.
answers.evidence: India terminology > empire definition and last-dominated-region rule.

answers.answer: 1. Final VP per firm share is: Value 1 = −1; Value 2 = 0; Values 3–4 = ½; Values 5–7 = 1; Values 8–9 = 1½; Value 10 = 2.
answers.evidence: Scoring > Firm-track VP per share.

answers.answer: 1. The Chairman title holder takes the first Family action, and other players act clockwise. After all Family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one, repeating while both remain; with no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving order.
answers.evidence: Family phase opening and New Company shares paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. Company offices operate along the red ribbon in this order: Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay Presidency → Madras Presidency → Bengal Presidency → China Superintendent, if created. Skip each vacant office. Within each Presidency, its President chooses the order of Commander, Governors and Trade, and each position finishes before the next acts. Each office spends only its own treasury.
answers.evidence: Company Operation sequence and Presidency-order paragraph.

answers.answer: 1. First roll the storm die; its face specifies affected sea zones and the number of India events. Resolve all required storms before drawing any event. Company and extra ships are exempt from storm checks; check player-owned ships in Company fleets in affected sea zones; China ships count as Eastern; firm ships count in the sea zone on their firm strategy; Hobnob ships are exempt. Roll once per eligible ship: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink, returning sunk ships to their shipyards unfatigued. 2. Then flip and resolve one tile at a time from the draw stack, for as many events as the number printed on the storm die face. Where an event uses a region, normally read the back of the new top tile, not the tile just drawn, subject to its specific location rule.
answers.evidence: Events in India opening storm/event sequence and Storms table (“Company and extra ships” exempt; “Ships assigned to China” count Eastern; one roll per eligible ship).

answers.answer: 1. For an ordinary Crisis event, the Elephant’s tail is the attacker/acting region and its head is the defender. A sovereign actor causes Invasion; a dominated actor causes Rebellion against its sovereign. If the Elephant is wholly inside a Company region, resolve Rebellion against the Company. Sovereign regions have a dome without a flag or a capital/star flag; dominated regions have a small flag or no dome.
answers.evidence: Events in India > ordinary Crisis classifier; India terminology.
